subject: Weekly readout: pipeline-linked reserve scaler + contingency runbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Cho <sam@orbitai.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finance-orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly readout: pipeline-linked reserve scaler + contingency runbook

Team —

Running the weekly sizing pass for deals that are asking to convert pilots into reserved capacity. I pulled the latest pipeline forecast from HubSpot and ran the reserve-sizer (attached) with three scenarios: conservative (60% conversion), base (75%), upside (90%). Key asks:

- Kimberly: take a look at the assumed run-rate per seat for OrbitAI (tab: ORBIT) — finance will push on the ARR/RPU assumptions.
- Ben: confirm burst eligibility and how many reserved slots we can map to OrbitAI by product (inference vs. embeddings).
- Jordan: validate infra constraints for Q3 (GPU procurement lead time and pool fragility).

Immediate highlights from the base scenario: OrbitAI demand maps to ~48 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent) in month 2 of conversion, with a soft peak of 72 if they exercise early-burst. If we layer on our autoscale buffer (15%) and safety pool mapping rules, that suggests recommending a 60-GPU reserved contract with a 20-GPU burst window.

Notes in the spreadsheet: an expected 8-week procurement lead time if we need to spin new capacity; fallback path to regional routing and smaller model variants included in the runbook. I've also added a suggested line for a 3-month canary where we gradually shift traffic and run GA benchmarks.

Attaching: pipeline_sizer_v3.xlsx and reserved-contingency-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook has the playbook for mutual action plan items).

Please reply with confirmations or edits by EOD Thursday so I can update the customer-facing MGP and the finance forecast.

—Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finance-orbitai.com>, Sam Cho <sam@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly readout: pipeline-linked reserve scaler + contingency runbook

Thanks Marcus — quick notes after a first pass on ORBIT tab:

- Pricing assumption: their rep quoted an effective RPU that's 12% higher than the spreadsheet's baseline. If they stick to that, ARR math supports the 60-GPU ask — otherwise finance will ask for a stepped commitment.
- Billing cadence: they want net-30 but procurement indicated they may request net-45 for pilots converting to reserved. Recommend we prepare two billing scenarios in the forecast.
- Profitability: with the 60 GPU reserve + 20 burst, modeled margin stays above 35% under base conversion; downside scenario drops margin to 18% unless we increase model quantization or shift heavy users to off-peak windows.

Action: Marcus/Ben, add a column in the spreadsheet for a quantization / model-size remediation (e.g., 4-bit inference path) so we can show finance the options to recover margin.

Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sam Cho <sam@orbitai.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly readout: pipeline-linked reserve scaler + contingency runbook

Looping infra constraints in — quick infra read:

- Available spot of A100-equivalents next procurement window: 40 GPUs (regional pool). Vendor lead times still ~8 weeks as Marcus noted.
- Burst policy: we can carve a 20-GPU burst but only as preemptible instances without SLA; for guaranteed burst we need reserved capacity.
- Alternative: mix of reserved VMs (48 GPUs) + dedicated burst credits (20 GPUs preemptible) to hit the economic target while keeping guaranteed capacity to 48.

I'll update the spreadsheet with a separate sheet called "deploy_mix" that includes three mixes: guaranteed-heavy, economical-mix, and preemptible-first. Each has cost per token and expected P95 latency impact noted.

Ben

From: Sam Cho <sam@orbitai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finance-orbitai.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2029 11:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly readout: pipeline-linked reserve scaler + contingency runbook

Appreciate the detailed breakdown — a couple clarifications from OrbitAI's side:

- The 60 GPU request is the internal ask from our ML team based on expected production load. They are open to a blended approach if it reduces cost and doesn't blow up latency beyond 10% at P95.
- Procurement tempo: legal expects to sign a T&Cs addendum within two weeks if pricing is stable; finance (Priya) needs a clear ARR impact for Q3 planning.
- Can we start with a 30-day canary with 20 guaranteed GPUs and a second 30-day ramp to 60 if KPIs (cost per request, P95 latency, error rate) remain within thresholds?

If you can provide the canary playbook and the deployment_mix options, we can run that internally and come back with a final ask next Monday.

Sam

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Cho <sam@orbitai.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finance-orbitai.com>, cloudops@orbitai-corp.com
Date: Fri, 24 May 2029 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly readout: pipeline-linked reserve scaler + contingency runbook

Thanks all — next steps captured below (will push updated sheet + runbook by EOD Friday):

1) Marcus: add quantization delta column and three deployment_mix rows (guaranteed-heavy / economical-mix / preemptible-first).
2) Kimberly: prepare two finance forecasts (net-30 vs net-45) and model incremental margin recovery via quantization + off-peak throttling.
3) Ben/Jordan: validate procurement timing and confirm which part of the 60 GPUs must be reserved for guaranteed SLAs vs burst credits.
4) Sam/Priya: agree to 30/30 canary cadence; customer to confirm KPI thresholds by Monday 2029-05-27.

I'll attach the updated pipeline_sizer_v3.xlsx (rev B) and a concise canary runbook (reserved-contingency-runbook-v1.pdf) once changes are in. If anyone wants a short sync we can take 20 minutes tomorrow morning.
